composing_text: UK-INF-049D (the only division under command at first)
current_activity: Headquarters, arrived from Italy early in March, comes under First Canadian Army at midday with the 49th Division
notes: Event date: 15 March 1945, midday (Stacey, p. 545); the headquarters arrived from Italy early in March. Event definition: The corps headquarters, which arrived from Italy early in March, comes under General Crerar at midday on 15 March, at first with only the 49th (West Riding) Division under command, in the Arnhem sector; the 5th Armoured Division had begun to arrive in Belgium in the last days of February and the 1st Infantry Division came under the command of General Simonds at noon on 3 April (p. 529). Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 545: "The Corps Headquarters had arrived from Italy early in March, and had come under General Crerar at midday on the 15th of the month, in the first instance with"; "only the 49th (West Riding) Division under command". Location: Nijmegen area, Gelderland (existing place PL0554) with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is Nijmegen, standing for the corps sector in the Nijmegen-Arnhem area; it is not a headquarters position. Location support: Stacey says the corps is under the Army in the Arnhem sector (p. 545); it names no headquarters place. Commander: Lt.-Gen. C. Foulkes (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 664: 1st Canadian Corps, 10 Nov. 44 to 17 Jul. 45). Context: Only the time in the Western Front theatre is recorded; the corps positions in Italy before this are deliberately not written (Canadian Batch 2 scope).

current_activity: Operation Destroyer completed: the corps holds a 20-mile salient along the Neder Rijn and the Pannerdensch Canal
notes: Event date: 3 April 1945, evening (Stacey, p. 568). Event definition: On the evening of the day the island operation ends, the corps occupies a wide salient in the western Netherlands, a 20-mile stretch of the left bank of the Neder Rijn and the Pannerdensch Canal from the canal junction with the Waal to north-west of Randwijk, with Arnhem facing it across the river. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 568: "on the evening of 3 April General Foulkes' 1st Corps occupied a wide salient thrusting into the western Netherlands"; "a 20-mile stretch of the left bank of the Neder Rijn and the Pannerdensch Canal". Location: Arnhem area, Gelderland (existing place PL0553) with a precision of 25 km. Location approximate: the point is Arnhem, standing for the salient it faced; the corps headquarters place is not stated. Location support: Stacey describes the salient between the Pannerdensch Canal and Randwijk, opposite Arnhem (p. 568). Commander: Lt.-Gen. C. Foulkes (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 664: 1st Canadian Corps, 10 Nov. 44 to 17 Jul. 45). Context: Only the time in the Western Front theatre is recorded; the corps positions in Italy before this are deliberately not written (Canadian Batch 2 scope).

composing_text: UK-INF-049D (49th West Riding Division, whose assault took Arnhem)
current_activity: Corps orders to clear western Holland to the Grebbe Line; the 49th Division's Arnhem assault succeeds quickly
notes: Event date: 14 April 1945 (Stacey, pp. 572 and 574). Event definition: General Foulkes issues new orders to his divisional commanders, confirmed in writing on 15 April, for the corps to clear the enemy from western Holland between the Ijssel and the Grebbe Line; the 49th Division assault at Arnhem has succeeded quickly, so the 1st Division is ordered to link up with it and open the Arnhem-Zutphen road. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 572: "On 14 April, accordingly, General Foulkes in his turn issued new verbal orders to his divisional commanders, confirming them in writing on the 15th"; "1 Cdn Corps will clear enemy from Western Holland between the Ijssel and the Grebbe Line"; p. 574: "quick success attending the 49th Division's assault at Arnhem". Location: Arnhem, Gelderland (existing place PL0553) with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is Arnhem, the town taken that week; the corps headquarters place is not stated. Location support: Stacey names the 49th Division assault at Arnhem and the corps task west of the Ijssel (pp. 572-574). Commander: Lt.-Gen. C. Foulkes (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 664: 1st Canadian Corps, 10 Nov. 44 to 17 Jul. 45). Context: Only the time in the Western Front theatre is recorded; the corps positions in Italy before this are deliberately not written (Canadian Batch 2 scope).

current_activity: Corps headquarters moves forward to Harskamp, two miles north of Otterlo
notes: Event date: 22 April 1945 (Stacey, p. 587). Event definition: The corps headquarters moves forward to Harskamp, two miles north of Otterloo. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 587: "General Foulkes' headquarters moved forward to Harskamp, two miles north of Otterloo, on 22 April". Location: Harskamp, Gelderland with a precision of 5 km. Location support: Stacey names Harskamp for the headquarters move (p. 587). Commander: Lt.-Gen. C. Foulkes (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 664: 1st Canadian Corps, 10 Nov. 44 to 17 Jul. 45). Context: Only the time in the Western Front theatre is recorded; the corps positions in Italy before this are deliberately not written (Canadian Batch 2 scope).

current_activity: General Blaskowitz surrenders the German forces in the western Netherlands to General Foulkes at Wageningen
notes: Event date: 5 May 1945 (Stacey, p. 614). Event definition: General Blaskowitz surrenders to General Foulkes in a battered hotel at Wageningen, after General Foulkes reads out the terms of surrender; Stacey says Blaskowitz is responsible for the German forces in the area. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 614: "Blaskowitz had surrendered to General Foulkes in a battered hotel at Wageningen on the 5th"; "The terms of surrender were read over by General Foulkes". Location: Wageningen, Gelderland with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is the meeting place at Wageningen; the corps headquarters was at Harskamp from 22 April (p. 587) and is not stated for 5 May. Location support: Stacey names a hotel at Wageningen as the meeting place (p. 614). Commander: Lt.-Gen. C. Foulkes (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 664: 1st Canadian Corps, 10 Nov. 44 to 17 Jul. 45). Context: Only the time in the Western Front theatre is recorded; the corps positions in Italy before this are deliberately not written (Canadian Batch 2 scope).

composing_text: UK-INF-049D (took over the 88th German Corps area on 7 May); CAN-INF-001D (took control of the 30th German Corps area on 8 May)
current_activity: Corps enters western Holland: 49th Division at Utrecht on 7 May, 1st Division takes the western area on 8 May
notes: Event date: 7 May 1945 (Stacey, p. 614); the 1st Division part is dated 8 May. Event definition: The corps enters the western Netherlands on 7 May, when the 49th (West Riding) Division takes over the German 88th Corps area about Utrecht, from the Ijsselmeer to the Lek; on 8 May the 1st Canadian Division takes control of the German 30th Corps area in the remaining territory to the west, the route running through Amersfoort and Utrecht to Rotterdam. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 614: "The 1st Corps entered the western Netherlands on 7 May, when the 49th (West Riding) Division took over the 88th German Corps' area about Utrecht"; "On the 8th General Foster's 1st Canadian Division took control of the 30th German Corps' area in the remaining territory to the west". Location: Utrecht, Utrecht (existing place PL0621) with a precision of 25 km. Location approximate: the point is Utrecht, standing for the occupied area; the corps headquarters place is not stated. Location support: Stacey names Utrecht for the 49th Division area and the route through Amersfoort and Utrecht to Rotterdam for the 1st Division (p. 614). Commander: Lt.-Gen. C. Foulkes (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 664: 1st Canadian Corps, 10 Nov. 44 to 17 Jul. 45).
